title: Airbnb Booking System: Complete Architecture
description: Design a scalable Airbnb-style booking platform with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a scalable Airbnb-style short-term rental booking platform. The system must allow hosts to list properties with photos, descriptions, amenities, and pricing rules. Guests must be able to search by location, dates, and number of guests, view listing details, make reservations, process payments, and leave reviews. The platform also needs real-time calendar availability, messaging between hosts and guests, and dynamic pricing support.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Hosts can create, edit, and delete property listings with photo galleries, amenities, and house rules
Guests can search listings by city, check-in/check-out dates, price range, and property type
Guests can view detailed listing pages with photo carousels, maps, host info, and past reviews
Guests can make bookings with date selection, guest count, and special requests
Calendar availability must update in real-time when a booking is confirmed or cancelled
Secure payment processing with support for credit cards and refunds
Hosts and guests can exchange messages through an in-platform messaging system
Guests can leave reviews and ratings (1-5 stars) after checkout
Hosts can set dynamic pricing rules based on season, day of week, and local events
Users can save favorite listings to a wishlist

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Search results must load in under 500ms with filters for price, dates, and amenities
Booking creation must be atomic with no double-booking conflicts
Payment processing must meet PCI DSS compliance requirements
99.95% availability for the booking and payment flows
Listing photos must be optimized and served via CDN for fast loading
Calendar sync must be near real-time to prevent overlapping reservations
System must handle seasonal spikes (summer, holidays) with 5x normal traffic

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application where all domains—listings, bookings, payments, reviews, and messaging—share a single deployment and database. This is the fastest way to validate the Airbnb Booking domain model and transactional requirements.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API or MVC Controllers
  - Entity Framework Core for data access
  - Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
  - Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for listing photos
  - Azure Monitor or AWS CloudWatch for logging
  - Single database with tables for Listings, Bookings, Payments, Reviews, Messages

data.text: As traffic grows, split the monolith into independently scalable microservices. Each service owns its data and communicates via async messaging or REST/gRPC. Booking and payment services require strict consistency; search and notification services can tolerate eventual consistency.

items: Search Service: Handles location-based search, date filtering, price ranges, and amenity filters. Uses Elasticsearch or Azure Cognitive Search for full-text and geo-queries.
Listing Service: Manages property CRUD, photo uploads, amenities, pricing rules, and calendar availability. Publishes events when listings are created or updated.
Booking Service: Creates reservations, validates calendar conflicts, manages booking states (pending/confirmed/cancelled), and enforces cancellation policies.
Payment Service: Processes charges via Stripe or Braintree, handles refunds, webhooks for payment confirmation, and stores transaction records for PCI compliance.
Review Service: Collects guest reviews and star ratings after checkout, prevents duplicate reviews, and calculates average ratings for listings.
Messaging Service: Enables host-guest communication before and during stays, with notification triggers for new messages.
Notification Service: Sends email and push notifications for booking confirmations, payment receipts, message alerts, and review requests.

data.title: React App Structure
data.code:
src/
  features/
    airbnb-booking/
      search/           # Map view, filters, results grid
      listing/           # Photo gallery, amenities, host info, reviews
      booking/           # Date picker, guest count, checkout flow
      payments/          # Secure payment form with Stripe Elements
      messages/          # Threaded chat UI
      profile/           # User profile, wishlist, trip history
      hosts/             # Host dashboard, listing creation
      api/               # API clients per service
      components/        # Shared UI components
      hooks/             # Custom hooks
      store/             # Zustand/Jotai state
      types/             # TypeScript interfaces
  shared/
    ui/                 # Design system
    lib/                 # Utilities
    hooks/               # Global hooks

Key Patterns:
  - Map-based search with Leaflet or Mapbox for geo-filtering
  - Debounced search queries to reduce API calls
  - Optimistic UI for booking confirmations with rollback
  - Image lazy-loading and progressive loading for photo galleries
  - React Query for caching search results and listing details
  - WebSocket for real-time messaging notifications

data.title: Booking Service (ASP.NET Core)

cards.title: Compute
cards.description: Host booking and payment API containers
cons: Cold start latency for serverless functions

cards.title: API Gateway
cards.description: Route search, booking, and payment requests
cons: Additional cost and latency per request

cards.title: Cache
cards.description: Cache hot listings, search filters, and user sessions
pros: Sub-millisecond access to frequently viewed listings
cons: Eviction can cause cache stampede during spikes

cards.title: Database
cards.description: Primary data store for bookings, listings, and users
pros: Strong ACID guarantees for bookings and payments
cons: Vertical scaling limits; requires read replicas for scale

cards.title: Storage
cards.description: Store listing photos, host documents, and media
pros: Integrated CDN for fast image delivery globally
cons: Eventual consistency for listing image updates

cards.title: Messaging
cards.description: Async events for booking, payment, and notifications
pros: Decouples booking from payment and notifications
Buffers traffic spikes during peak seasons
cons: Requires careful ordering for booking lifecycle events

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: Airbnb Booking System requires strong consistency for bookings and payments, but eventual consistency is acceptable for reviews and messaging
Calendar conflict detection is the hardest invariant—use database transactions or distributed locks
Payment processing must be idempotent to handle webhook retries safely
Photo CDN is critical for UX; listing pages with slow images have higher bounce rates
Start with a monolith on Azure SQL or AWS RDS, then extract Search, Booking, and Payment as the first microservices
data.takeaway: Airbnb Booking System is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
